object_description: two-building school ensemble with a raised sports hall
design_condition: The school extension moves east while the sports hall rises, preserving and slightly reworking the existing exterior concept.

positive.statement: The new volume is balanced and integrates naturally into the site.
The exterior layout refers appropriately to the current concept and is slightly reworked.
The distribution of premises between the three buildings is clear.
Removing rooms on the west side creates a generous meeting space with natural lighting.
The fire escapes in the annex are strategically well positioned.
The double-height study rooms generate additional spatial richness.
The cluster benefits from overhead lighting through skylights and double-height spaces.
The new facade gives the ensemble a contemporary expression.
The interventions on the main building show flexibility, elegance and spatial quality.

negative.statement: The aula seems too far away, and a more central location is desired.
Raising the sports hall requires demolishing the existing supporting structure and generates additional cost.
The decisive supporting system leaves some rooms with less-than-ideal proportions.
The rigid structure is not very flexible for possible subsequent modifications.
Using rooms to connect circulation between sectors is not judicious and calls the floor functioning into question.
Despite its interesting typology, the circulation system remains labyrinthine.
The visual connection of two floors is interesting but not obvious.
The elevation demonstrates the complexity and limits of organizing the triple sports hall.
